authors: David A. Weisberger; Marshall D. McDaniel; J. Gordon Arbuckle; Matt Liebman et al.
title: Farmer perspectives on benefits of and barriers to extended crop rotations in Iowa, USA
region_crops: US Iowa; maize, soybean, small grains
problem_stated: Farmers see soil benefits of extended rotations (83% agree) but rate structural barriers highest: lack of markets 82%, land rents 81%, genetics 65%, technical support 59%, equipment 58%. Only 28% agree extended rotations can be as profitable; 41% uncertain. 75% rate documentation of long-term profitability important.

authors: Matthew Nowatzke; Lijing Gao; Michael C. Dorneich; Emily A. Heaton et al.
title: Interviews with farmers from the US corn belt highlight opportunity for improved decision support systems and continued structural barriers to farmland diversification
region_crops: US Iowa/Illinois; maize, soybean, small grains, CRP
problem_stated: Farmers who diversified need multi-year layered data (yield, soil maps, satellite imagery, elevation), financial information and goal matching; current tools are clunky, costly, tied to equipment brands and ignore conservation, profitability and soil health. Markets, crop insurance, rented land, social pressure and agency relations are barriers a tool cannot fix. Public soil maps described as hit-or-miss. Small sample (11).

authors: Hazem S. Kassem; Abdel Raouf Suleiman Bello; Bader M. Alotaibi; Fahd O. Aldosri et al.
title: Climate Change Adaptation in the Delta Nile Region of Egypt: Implications for Agricultural Extension
region_crops: Egypt Nile Delta (Kafr El-Sheikh, El-Beheira); mixed
problem_stated: 51.9% of farmers had no knowledge of climate change; 31.7% illiterate; 70.3% farm 10 feddan or less. Reported effects: lower productivity 84.5%, pests and diseases 81.4%, soil salinity 57.2%, higher water requirements 25.7%. 76.3% changed crop pattern/rotation. Information mainly from sons (59.6%) and TV (33.7%); extension 13.5%. Extension contact had no significant effect on adoption.

authors: Eman S. Swelam; M. R. Abdallah; Hamed Abdelreheem Ead; Attia M. El-Tantawi et al.
title: Climate change perception–impact–adaptation pathways among farmers: evidence from seven major agricultural governorates in Egypt
problem_stated: Crop rotation is near-universal (96.6%). Only 3.6% receive climate guidance from government extension; 47.1% rely on peers. Barriers: capital cost 49.3%, uncertainty about effectiveness of practices 33.6%, input costs 26.1%, water scarcity 21.8%. Digital tools: 3.9% full use, 23.1% unfamiliar. 84.6% want awareness programmes. Authors describe an information-poverty trap.

authors: Wafa Ghazouani; François Molle; Atef Swelam; Edwin Rap et al.
title: Understanding farmers’ adaptation to water scarcity: a case study from the western Nile Delta, Egypt
venue: CGSPace A Repository of Agricultural Research Outputs (Consultative Group for International Agricultural Research)
region_crops: Egypt western Nile Delta (al-Bayda canal); rice, maize, cotton, vegetables, grapes
datasets: farmer surveys along one branch canal
problem_stated: Water shortage grows toward canal tail ends: in one tail location 58% said rice became very difficult and 50% gave up vegetables; reported yield drops of about 25% (rice, maize) to 30-50% (rice). Farmers buy extra pumps and reuse saline drainage water. Upstream farmers are bound to frequent rice for salinity control, which raises the water table and rules out other crops.

authors: Samar M. Attaher; MAHMOUD A. MEDANY; Ayman Farid Abou-Hadid
title: Possible adaptation measures of agriculture sector in the Nile Delta to climate change impacts
problem_stated: Vulnerability attributed to sea level rise, soil and water degradation, undiversified crop pattern, yield reduction, pests, and irrigation and drainage management. Farmers want a clear scientific message and government support. Short conference paper.

authors: Mohammed Hagage; Abdulaziz M. Abdulaziz; Salwa Farouk Elbeih; Abdel Galil A. Hewaidy et al.
title: Monitoring soil salinization and waterlogging in the northeastern Nile Delta linked to shallow saline groundwater and irrigation water quality
datasets: soil and water samples, Sentinel-2, SRTM
problem_stated: 64% of soil samples strongly or very strongly saline; 87.5% of irrigation water samples under severe restriction; shallow saline groundwater at 0.5-3 m; waterlogging in northern lowlands. Does not survey farmers.

authors: Saher Ayyad; Poolad Karimi; Lars Ribbe; M. Becker et al.
title: Potential Improvements in Crop Production in Egypt and Implications for Future Water and Land Demand
region_crops: Egypt, Zankalon (Nile Delta); rice, maize, wheat, berseem
problem_stated: Rice, maize, wheat and berseem take about half of harvested area and renewable freshwater. Yield gaps up to 27%. Describes Egypt as water- and data-scarce. Does not survey farmers.

authors: Lauren Asprooth; Margaret Krome; Alyssa Hartman; Ashley McFarland et al.
title: Our daily bread in the Heartland: Understanding and leveraging diversification to small grains in corn and soybean systems
venue: Journal of Soil and Water Conservation
region_crops: US Iowa, Illinois, Minnesota, Wisconsin; small grains in maize-soybean
problem_stated: Among farmers who never grew or stopped growing small grains: low prices 45% and lack of markets 43% are the main barriers; technical assistance (2%) and crop insurance (4%) rarely selected. Timing of planting and harvest, equipment and varieties cut both ways.

authors: Lauren Asprooth; J. Gordon Arbuckle; Rebecca Traldi; Sarah P. Church et al.
title: To diversify or not to diversify: a preliminary report on farmers’ perspectives on diversification in the U.S. Midwest
problem_stated: Farmers see mainly economic barriers to diversification: lack of affordable land, low short-term returns, lack of labour. Farmers ask for more information on returns on investment. Over 80% disagree or are neutral that their community supports diversified agriculture.

authors: Yvonne Socolar; Benjamin R. Goldstein; Perry de Valpine; Timothy M. Bowles et al.
title: Biophysical and policy factors predict simplified crop rotations in the US Midwest
datasets: USDA CDL, land capability, precipitation, distance to biofuel plants
problem_stated: Rotations are simplest on the best land and near biofuel plants; rotation complexity rises with lower growing-season precipitation and poorer land. Field-level rotation patterns were largely unstudied at regional scale.

authors: Suraj Upadhaya; J. Gordon Arbuckle
title: Examining Factors Associated With Farmers' Climate-Adaptive and Maladaptive Actions in the U.S. Midwest
problem_stated: Reliance on crop insurance is associated with maladaptive responses to weather extremes (more pesticide) and may discourage practices that risk short-term yield.

authors: Dan M. Kluger; Stefania Di Tommaso; David B. Lobell
title: Precrop payoffs: causal machine learning reveals large but variable yield benefits of crop rotation in major breadbaskets
region_crops: US, Canada, other breadbaskets; maize, soybean, wheat
datasets: crop type maps, satellite yield, weather
problem_stated: States a knowledge gap on how rotation benefits vary by sequence and weather. Finds common precrops are among the most beneficial; moving from a 2-crop to a more diverse rotation gave small and sometimes negative yield effects; legume precrop benefit smaller under warmer conditions.

authors: E. A. Sutton; Meha Jain; Kent Connell; Haoyu Wang et al.
title: Increasing crop rotation diversity with cover crops builds climate resilience on farms
region_crops: US Michigan; maize, soybean, cover crops
problem_stated: Heavy spring rain disrupts planting and summer drought is more intense. Cover crop benefits for yield stability take several years to appear, so farmers face more variable yields early on.

authors: Leah L.R. Renwick; William Deen; Lucas C. R. Silva; Matthew E. Gilbert et al.
title: Long-term crop rotation diversification enhances maize drought resistance through soil organic matter
region_crops: US (long-term trial with rainout shelters); maize
problem_stated: Diversified rotation cut maize yield loss to drought by 17.1% but the mechanism was not the expected one (not infiltration or water retention).

authors: Monique E. Smith; Giulia Vico; Alessio Costa; Timothy M. Bowles et al.
title: Increasing crop rotational diversity can enhance cereal yields
region_crops: Europe and North America, 32 long-term experiments
problem_stated: Rotational diversity raises cereal yields over time, but farmers have a limited set of crops and must weigh the yield benefit against market value, skills, infrastructure and soils.

authors: David Christian Rose; William J. Sutherland; Caroline Parker; Matt Lobley et al.
title: Decision support tools for agriculture: Towards effective design and delivery
problem_stated: Uptake of decision support tools is low despite many tools; 49% of farmers used any tool. Fifteen factors drive use, including usability, cost-effectiveness, performance, relevance to the user, trust and compliance needs.

authors: Gabrielle Elan Roesch-McNally; J. Gordon Arbuckle; John Tyndall
title: Barriers to implementing climate resilient agricultural strategies: The case of crop diversification in the U.S. Corn Belt
problem_stated: Abstract: path dependency of the corn-based system limits diverse rotations; farmers with livestock or marginal land rotate more.

authors: Timothy M. Bowles; Maria Mooshammer; Yvonne Socolar; Francisco J. Calderón et al.
title: Long-Term Evidence Shows that Crop-Rotation Diversification Increases Agricultural Resilience to Adverse Growing Conditions in North America
access_status: ABSTRACT ONLY (open access, not yet read)
problem_stated: Abstract: more diverse rotations raised maize yields 28.1% on average and cut drought-year losses 14.0-89.9%.

authors: Ankit Shekhar; Charles A. Shapiro
title: What do meteorological indices tell us about a long-term tillage study?
problem_stated: Abstract: corn-soybean beat continuous corn by 28% in normal years, but continuous corn yielded 17% more under extreme or prolonged drought.

authors: Ankit Shekhar; Charles A. Shapiro
title: Prospective crop yield and income return based on a retrospective analysis of a long-term rainfed agriculture experiment in Nebraska
access_status: ABSTRACT ONLY (open access, not yet read)
problem_stated: Abstract: dry-summer years cut corn yield 38.6% and soybean 31.8%; corn-soybean more profitable and stable than continuous corn.

authors: T. H. S. Kotb; Tsugihiro Watanabe; Yoshihiko Ogino; Kenneth K. Tanji et al.
title: Soil salinization in the Nile Delta and related policy issues in Egypt
problem_stated: Abstract: rice helps control salinity in the northern Delta but is limited by water shortfalls and policy limits on rice area.

authors: Nader Noureldeen Mohamed
title: Management of Salt-Affected Soils in the Nile Delta
problem_stated: Abstract: salt-affected soils average 37% of cultivated Delta soils, up to 46% in the north.

authors: Tong Wang; Hailong Jin; Yubing Fan; Oladipo S. Obembe et al.
title: Farmers’ adoption and perceived benefits of diversified crop rotations in the margins of U.S. Corn Belt
problem_stated: Abstract: diversified rotation used to cope with water deficit and erosion on marginal land; equipment and profitability concerns reduce interest.

authors: Bishal Kasu; Jeffrey Jacquet; Anne N. Junod; Sandeep Kumar et al.
title: Rationale and Motivation of Agricultural Producers in Adopting Crop Rotation in the Northern Great Plains, USA
region_crops: US South Dakota, North Dakota, Nebraska
problem_stated: Abstract: profitability drives rotation adoption; lack of time or resources is the main barrier.

authors: Charles Andrew Francis; Humberto Blanco‐Canqui; Cody F. Creech
title: Adaptive rotations for improving soil productivity and profits
problem_stated: Abstract: adaptive rotations impeded by reluctance to change, complexity, leased land, subsidies, lender risk perception and lack of research results.

authors: K. Ann Bybee‐Finley; Katherine E. Muller; Kathryn E. White; Michel A. Cavigelli et al.
title: Rotational complexity increases cropping system output under poorer growing conditions
access_status: ABSTRACT ONLY (open access, not yet read)
problem_stated: Abstract: adoption limited by economic uncertainty, lack of incentives and limited information on long-term outcomes; diverse rotations reduced rotation-level output at 8 sites.

authors: Alessio Costa; Riccardo Bommarco; Monique E. Smith; Timothy M. Bowles et al.
title: Crop rotational diversity can mitigate climate‐induced grain yield losses
access_status: ABSTRACT ONLY (open access, not yet read)
problem_stated: Abstract: diverse rotations offset yield losses from warm and dry anomalies; benefit peaks at 2-4 species.

authors: Gregg A. Johnson; Robert Ford Denison; Jeffrey S. Strock; Samantha Wells et al.
title: Maize productivity and yield stability in diversified cropping systems: Insights from a long‐term regional network
problem_stated: Abstract: 3-crop rotation yielded most on average but less in drought years at two sites; benefits are site-specific.

authors: Ahmed Fahmy; Radwa Maher. Ata

problem_stated: Abstract: farmers rate hydro-climatic variability high and the quality of available information poor; want accurate, timely, trusted information.

authors: Adham Badawy; Amgad Elmahdi; Sayed A. Abd El-Hafez; Ali Ibrahim et al.
title: Water Profitability Analysis to Improve Food Security and Climate Resilience: A Case Study in the Egyptian Nile Delta
access_status: ABSTRACT ONLY (open access, not yet read)
problem_stated: Abstract: lack of extension limits land and water productivity; small parcels.

authors: Ahmed Abdalla; Till Stellmacher; M. Becker
title: Wheat Farmers’ Perception of Constraints and Their Adaptive Capacity to Changing Demands in Egypt
access_status: ABSTRACT ONLY (open access, not yet read)
problem_stated: Abstract: wheat area decisions driven by home consumption, livestock, and government price and its announcement time; poor extension and markets.

authors: Samiha A. H. Ouda; Tahany Noreldin; Khaled Abd El-Latif
title: Water requirements for wheat and maize under climate change in North Nile Delta
region_crops: Egypt north Nile Delta; wheat, maize
problem_stated: Abstract: water requirements projected to rise 2-3% for wheat and 10-15% for maize by 2040.

authors: Bezaiet Dessalegn; Eman Abd-Allah; Shaban Salem; Atef Swelam et al.
title: Explaining shifts in adaptive water management using a gendered multi-level perspective (MLP): a case study from the Nile Delta of Egypt
problem_stated: Abstract: water management choices shaped by interacting local, institutional and global drivers, with gender differences.

authors: Boubaker Dhehibi
title: The Baseline Analysis of the Nile Delta of Egypt
venue: MELSpace (ICARDA (The International Center for Agricultural Research in Dry Areas))
problem_stated: Abstract: holdings 1-2 feddan in old lands; illiteracy 18-33%; weak credit, inputs and markets; asks which crops give most value per unit land and water.

authors: Reda M. Amer
title: Spatial Relationship between Irrigation Water Salinity, Waterlogging, and Cropland Degradation in the Arid and Semi-Arid Environments
access_status: ABSTRACT ONLY (open access, not yet read)
problem_stated: Abstract: saline irrigation groundwater linked to soil salinity and waterlogging.

title: Improving water resources management efficiency under arid regions conditions based on simulation model technique
problem_stated: Abstract: about 836 million m3/year of drainage water reused unofficially by farmers; average soil salinity 2.55 dS/m.

authors: So Pyay Thar; Thiagarajah Ramilan; Robert J. Farquharson; Deli Chen et al.
title: Identifying Potential for Decision Support Tools through Farm Systems Typology Analysis Coupled with Participatory Research: A Case for Smallholder Farmers in Myanmar
access_status: ABSTRACT ONLY (open access, not yet read)
problem_stated: Abstract: prescriptive tools do not match what many farmers want; they prefer discussion and familiar platforms.

problem_stated: Abstract: concerns about decision support systems are cost, knowledge, confidence, security and privacy.

title: Involving stakeholders in agricultural decision support systems: Improving user-centred design
venue: UEA Digital Repository (University of East Anglia)
